4. The Insurance company aggrieved over the award by the Tribunal, has filed the present appeal questioning their liability and quantum.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the insurance policy was a basic third party package which covered only third party own damages and personal accident coverage and the policy along with terms and conditions which was marked as Ex.R1.
The Tribunal ought to have followed the judgment report in 2020 (1) TN MAC 547 where it was held that the policy of the insurance being contractual.
The claimant is entitled to claim compensation only with reference to the terms and conditions of the policy and not beyond that.
The disability sufferred is not covered under the table given in Section IV personal Accident cover for owner-driver in the conditions of the policy of insurance.
Hence, this Court may allow the appeal by setting aside the award passed by the Tribunal.

6. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent submitted that the after considering the entire materials and witnesses, the Tribunal awarded compensation to the claimant, which is just and proper and the same does not need interference.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondent and perused the materials available on record.
8.
It is seen that the claimant as the owner of the car while travelling from Chidambaram  Jeyankondam Highways met with the accident due to the negligence of his driver.

The claimant sustained grievous injuries in the accident and therefore filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
The claimant was the owner of the vehicle and as such she could not be considered as a Thirty Party.
The policy was a package policy covering liability to third party and also for the owner/driver.

9. According to the learned counsel for the Insurance Company, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (

The injured claimant is a tort-feaser and she is not a third The Manager vs A.Bhuvaneswari on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107945124/

The policy as far as the claimant is considered is contractual in nature and therefore the compensation is payable only in terms and conditions of the policy.
According to the learned counsel, the injuries sustained by the claimant were not covered by the policy and as such the Insurance Company was not liable to pay the compensation.

10. The learned counsel relied on the Judgment in the case of Royal Sundaram Allianz Insurance Company Limited Vs. Somu (cited supra), and submitted that the terms and conditions for Package Policy are standard and hence relied on the extract of the conditions of the Policy referred to therein to support her submission that the injuries suffered by the claimant were not covered by the Package Policy.

sentences.text: In the said judgment, the conditions of the Policy are extracted and they are as follows.

Section IV  Personal Accident Cover for Owner- Driver, which reads as under:-
SECTION IV  PERSONAL ACCIDENT COVER FOR OWNER-DRIVER Subject otherwise to the Terms, Exceptions, Conditions and Limitations of this Policy, the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 19/03/2025 03:50:50 pm )

Company undertakes to pay compensation as per the following scale for bodily injury/death sustained by the owner-driver of the vehicle in direct connection with the vehicle insured or whilst mounting into/dismounting from or travelling in the insured vehicle as a co-driver, caused by violent accidental external and visible means which independent of any other cause shall within six calendar months of such injury result in:
 Details of Injury Scale of Com  (i) Death 100% of CSI (ii) Loss of two limbs or sight of two eyes or one 100% of CSI limb and sight of one eye (iii) Loss of one limb or sight of one eye 100% of CSI (iv) Permanent Total Disablement from injuries 100% of CSI other than named above.
The above said conditions of the policy apply to the present case also as the conditions are standard.
11. In the present case, it is seen that the claimant sustained 25% injury and therefore the learned counsel is right in her submission that the injuries sustained by the claimant are not covered by the policy.
It is trite that the policy of the Insurance as far as the coverage to owner/driver is https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 19/03/2025 03:50:50 pm ) concerned is purely contractual in nature, in contrast to the coverage for third parties which is statutory in nature.

sentences.text:
The Tribunal therefore erred in not considering the terms of the Policy, this Court is fortified in the said view by the Judgment of this Hon'ble Court reported in 2020 (1) TN MAC 547, wherein it was held as follows:
9.Reading of the conditions stipulated in the Policy with reference to Personal Accident Cover for Owner-Driver, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Tribunal has committed an error in not considering the nature of the Policy.

Contrarily, the Tribunal proceeded on the ground that there is a coverage of Policy and the Respondent- Claimant sustained injuries and taken treatment and therefore,
the Respondent-Claimant is entitled for Compensation.
The Tribunal is bound to see the nature of the Policy and the coverage as well as the terms and conditions stipulated in the Policy.

12. Therefore, in my view, if the conditions of the policy do not cover the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant, then the liability cannot be mulcted on the insurance company even if additional p r e m i u m w a s p a i d f o r p e r s o n a l a c c i d e n t c o v e r a g e . I n t h e l i g h t o f t h e a b o v e
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 19/03/2025 03:50:50 pm ) discussion,
This Court is of the view that the appeal deserves to be allowed.
13.It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the award passed by the Tribunal has been deposited before the Tribunal, in pursuance of the order passed by this Hon'ble Court.
The appellant Insurance Company is permitted to withdraw the said amount.

14. Further, the policy of contract between the appellant and the respondent is the Package Policy,
which does not provide for coverage in respect of the owner.
Further, it is the stand of the appellant that towards personal accident cover for the owner, only in the result of death or amputation, there is coverage.
In the case on hand, due to the accident, the respondent sustained injuries.
Such being the case, the respondent being not a third party and also have personal accident cover, the insurer of the vehicle cannot be made liable to pay the compensation.

15.Accordingly, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed, the Judgment and decree dated 16.06.2020 in M.C.O.P.No.190 of 2017 on the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
19/03/2025 03:50:50 pm ) file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Subordinate Judge),
Jayankondam is set aside.
